properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-26: an install redirected into a scratch folder (REFLOW2_BIN_DIR / REFLOW2_KIT_DIR) still registered reflow2 machine-wide in the real $HOME, and the user-wide loop-nudge hooks ran a scratch copy of the v0.66.0 kit for four days
properties.statement:
OBSERVED 2026-09-26 in a dev_reflow2 hub session: all four user-wide loop-nudge hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json (SessionStart, PostToolUse ×2, Stop) ran `python3 "/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ajs7-project-flo2/a638af14-cd8c-4876-825b-e0e4c3c56660/scratchpad/ci-sim/kit/kit/tools/loop_nudge.py"`, the v0.66.0 kit (files dated 2026-09-20) inside another session's scratch folder, not the current script (it differs from tools/loop_nudge.py at main a0d6b49). It was noticed only because the Stop hook's message printed its own path.

═══ WHAT WROTE IT (measured, from the session transcript) ═══
flo2 session a638af14, 2026-09-22T15:28Z, simulating CI, ran
`REFLOW2_VERSION=v0.66.0 REFLOW2_BIN_DIR=$S/bin REFLOW2_KIT_DIR=$S/kit sh -c "$(curl … tools/install.sh)" 2>&1 | tail -6`
with the stated intent "leaves ~/.local/bin/reflow2 alone". install.sh's machine-wide step (lines 162-176) runs `reflow2_install.py --binary $BIN_DIR/reflow2-mcp` unconditionally. reflow2_install.py honours REFLOW2_BIN_DIR for its `reflow2` wrapper only; the MCP registration, the slash commands and the hooks go to the real $HOME, and the hook command names the kit it runs from. So the redirect isolated two of the install's writes and not the rest. `tail -6` hid the lines that said so, and the session checked only the file it was worried about, ~/.local/bin/reflow2, which was indeed untouched.

CANDIDATES RULED OUT: a hand edit of settings.json (across every saved session transcript on this machine, the only tool calls naming the ci-sim folder are that install, a test run, and this session's own reads and repair); a deliberate install from that kit (the transcript states the opposite intent); a misreading (the file was read directly, and `reflow2 install --check` reported the hooks as needing an update until they were repointed). NOT REPRODUCED: install.sh was not re-run against a fake HOME; the mechanism is read from the code and matched to the transcript.

═══ ⭐ THE CLASS ═══
An install whose destination is redirected by environment variables READS as isolated and is not. A scratch folder is temporary, so every write that escaped the redirect ends up pointing at something that will vanish or go stale: here a kit four days behind, whose hooks fired in every Claude Code session on the machine. This is the same family as fact:the-machine-wide-installer-writes-configs-for-harnesses-you-do-not-have (the installer writes $HOME config nobody asked for), reached by a different road.

═══ INFERRED, NOT ESTABLISHED ═══
The same run probably also registered the user-scope `reflow2` MCP server with the scratch v0.66.0 binary. That would explain the "stray 0.66.0 shared server started from another session's CI-simulation scratch binary" that held cure's store on 2026-09-25 (recorded in the dev_reflow2 hub's note on its cure dependency). The registration now names /home/ajs7/project/reflow2/target/release/reflow2-mcp; this session did not find which session re-registered it, and the truncated output does not show the original registration.

═══ CONTAINED ON THIS MACHINE, 2026-09-26; THE CLASS IS OPEN ═══
The four hook commands in ~/.claude/settings.json were repointed to `python3 "/home/ajs7/project/reflow2/tools/loop_nudge.py"`, exactly what reflow2_install.py from this checkout writes (hook_command(nudge_script())), and `reflow2 install --check` then reported "hooks already current". Only the hooks were touched: a full `reflow2 install` would also have rewritten the hand-edited ~/.local/bin/reflow2, the slash commands and the OpenCode config. Nothing stops the next redirected install doing the same. Candidate fixes, NOT decided: (a) install.sh skips the machine-wide step when REFLOW2_KIT_DIR or REFLOW2_BIN_DIR is set, and says so; (b) an explicit opt-out (e.g. REFLOW2_NO_REGISTER=1) for CI and simulations; (c) reflow2_install.py refuses to write $HOME config that points into a temporary directory. Whichever it is, pin it with a test that runs install.sh with the redirects and a fake HOME, and asserts that nothing under that HOME was written.
